writeup.p: C02PacketUseEntity is the only serverbound channel in 1.8.9 by which the client tells the server it interacted with an entity. The wire form is a VarInt entityId, a VarInt enum action (INTERACT, ATTACK, INTERACT_AT) and, for INTERACT_AT only, three floats for the hit position on the target. Every attack, mount, item-frame edit and armor-stand manipulation goes through it. Because the packet carries no position, rotation or timestamp, the server validates it purely against its own copy of player and entity state, which is exactly what makes it trivial to spoof from a modified client.

NetHandlerPlayServer.processUseEntity resolves the target from the packet's entity id, then enforces a distance gate: squared distance must be under 36.0 (6 blocks) when the target is visible to the player, or 9.0 (3 blocks) when it is not. INTERACT routes to playerEntity.interactWith, INTERACT_AT to the per-vector entity handler, and ATTACK first kicks the player for targeting EntityItem, EntityXPOrb, EntityArrow or self ("Attempting to attack an invalid entity"), then calls attackTargetEntityWithCurrentItem. There is no rate limit and no attack-cooldown validation; the 1.8.9 swing cooldown is enforced only client-side in PlayerControllerMP and EntityPlayerSP.

All eight clients ship combat modules that live on this packet. Aura and KillAura variants send ATTACK in every client: Memeware and Nekoware split Single/Multi/Hypixel/Switch auras, Rise 5.99 and 6.x use Aura and KillAura, Sigma, Spicy and Tenacity each have Killaura modules. Criticals exists in Memeware, Nekoware, Rise 5.99, Sigma and Spicy, injecting C04 offset packets before the ATTACK. TPAura and TeleportAura in Memeware, Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x and Tenacity walk the server-side player to the target before attacking. ComboOneHit (Rise 5.99 and 6.x) floods ATTACK packets, and Spicy's TriggerBot and Wtap round out the combat surface. Freecam (Rise), Infinite (Rise 5.99), WorldGuardRegen, GodMode and AntiFireBall (Rise 6.x), PlayerHacks (Rise 5.99) and Sigma's AntiFreeze all filter or forge C02 as a secondary effect.

The server trusts three things: the entity id, the distance, and the action. Attack rate is unbounded, so ComboOneHit's 50-1000 packet bursts are legal wire traffic. INTERACT_AT's hitVec is client-chosen and unvalidated, which is why Sigma and Spicy Killaura spam INTERACT_AT with random hitVecs plus INTERACT as a disabler sequence, and why Rise 5.99's BedwarsTP can mount entities from outside reach. Friend protection is purely a client courtesy: Rise 5.99's Aura consults its friends list, Sigma's Killaura checks FriendManager.isFriend, Tenacity's KillAuraModule checks FriendCommand.isFriend, but nothing server-side knows about friends, so a client that skips the check can hit anyone. Anti-cheats counter with reach math, attack-rate caps, rotation-motion correlation, and ghost-interact detection.

overview: The combat funnel of 1.8.9: a VarInt entity id and an action enum are all the server needs to apply damage. KillAura family targets and attacks, Criticals injects C04 fall arcs ahead of the ATTACK, TPAura teleports the server-side player to the target first, ComboOneHit floods the channel, and TriggerBot/Wtap automate the last bits of the attack loop. Friend protection exists only inside the aura target filters, never as a standalone module, across the 8 clients.
server_handling: processUseEntity runs on the main thread via PacketThreadUtil and calls markPlayerActive, which resets the idle-kick timer. The entity lookup uses packetIn.getEntityFromWorld(worldServerForDimension(player.dimension)). Distance is checked as squared distance: 36.0 when canEntityBeSeen passes, 9.0 otherwise, with no horizontal/vertical split and no per-axis clamp. For ATTACK the invalid-target kick fires before any damage is dealt. There is no vanilla per-tick attack limit: the swing cooldown and the 20-tick hit cooldown live in client-side code (PlayerControllerMP.attackEntity and EntityPlayer.attackEntityAsMob), so a forged client can emit arbitrarily many attacks per tick and the server will process them all.
protocol_notes: The action is serialized with readEnumValue/writeEnumValue, a VarInt ordinal (0=INTERACT, 1=ATTACK, 2=INTERACT_AT). INTERACT_AT adds three floats read after the enum; the other two actions carry no payload, so the packet length varies by action. The Entity-based constructors resolve the entity id at construction time (entity.getEntityId), so modules that queue C02 after the target dies or unloads send a stale id that the server resolves to null and silently ignores. The Vec3 constructor always selects INTERACT_AT. The packet is registered at 0x02 in the SERVERBOUND play state table.
anticheat_landscape: NCP flags reach by comparing the server-side player position against the target at ATTACK time and tracks hit rates per second; ComboOneHit-style floods are its primary target. Rotation-aware checks flag attacks whose preceding C05/C06 rotation does not point at the target, which is why Memeware-style auras that send ATTACK without a rotation packet get flagged on newer anti-cheats while rotation-injecting auras pass. The INTERACT_AT plus INTERACT disabler sequence (Sigma, Spicy) is detected by anti-cheats that count ghost interacts. TPAura is trivially caught by movement checks, because the unconfirmed C04 walk trips the vanilla 'moved too quickly' math when the path is skipped. Friend checks are invisible to the server and exist purely as client-side target filtering.

modules.name: Aura / KillAura
modules.purpose: Select a target within reach and emit C02 ATTACK packets at a controlled rate, with optional autoblock around the attack.
modules.how_it_works: Target selection from client-side entity lists (CombatUtil.getTarget in Memeware, PlayerUtil.getEntities in Rise), aim injected into the motion event so the outgoing C05/C06 carries the rotation, then ATTACK fired through the client's packet path. Memeware's SingleAura alternates C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM and C08 placement at a fake BlockPos to block between attacks. Friend filtering happens inside target selection: Rise 5.99 checks its friends list, Sigma checks FriendManager.isFriend, Tenacity checks FriendCommand.isFriend.
modules.vanilla_hook: UpdateEvent (aim + attack trigger); the attack itself goes through PacketUtil.sendPacket so PacketOutEvent listeners see it.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Reach is measured server-side, so range settings above 3 blocks are the primary flag; auras that skip rotation injection fail rotation checks on NCP/Verus-class anti-cheats. The autoblock C07/C08 pair around each attack is a visible packet pattern.
modules.variations: Nekoware splits Single, Multi and Switch auras, all sending ATTACK via sendQueue or PacketUtil. Rise 5.99's Aura is a single 1100+ line module with PacketUtil.sendPacket, and its friends list gates targets at attack time. Rise 6.x KillAura uses PacketUtil.send and includes the InteractEntityFix component for ViaVersion. Sigma and Spicy Killaura both add the INTERACT_AT random-hitVec plus INTERACT disabler sequence after the attack. Tenacity KillAuraModule uses mc.getNetHandler().addToSendQueue.

modules.name: Criticals
modules.purpose: Force every melee hit to register as a critical by injecting C04 position packets that recreate the falling-jump arc immediately before the ATTACK.
modules.how_it_works: A PacketOutEvent handler waits for C02 with ACTION ATTACK, then queues C04 packets at y+0.1232225 (onGround false), y+1.0554E-9 (false) and y (true), rate-limited by a 320ms timer so the burst cannot fire twice inside one attack. The server applies fall-damage math to the reported arc, so the attack lands as a crit. Ground-spoof variants instead mutate the motion event's Y and ground flag with a decaying 0.001 offset so every movement packet looks like a fresh fall.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketOutEvent on outgoing C02 ATTACK; UpdateEvent for the ground-spoof mode.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Packet criticals are detected by checking that the vertical offsets match the jump parabola and that the attack follows the offset burst within a tick window; the 0.1232225 value is a fingerprint shared across clients. Ground-spoof criticals leave a visible Y oscillation but pass offset-matching checks.
modules.variations: Nekoware's Criticals is the same file lineage with identical offsets. Rise 5.99 sends C04 at y+0.0625 and y+0.0 through PacketUtil.sendPacket. Sigma sends C06PacketPlayerPosLook offset pairs with a 1E-11 micro-offset on the second leg. Spicy sends C04 with randomized per-axis offsets and a RandomY term.

modules.name: TPAura / TeleportAura
modules.purpose: Attack entities far beyond reach by teleporting the server-side player to the target with a C04 path, attacking, and walking back.
modules.how_it_works: On PreMotionEvent, pick a target up to 120 blocks away, compute a path with a pathfinder, replay it as C04 position packets via sendPacketWithoutEvent (bypassing the event bus), fire the C02 ATTACK, then reverse the path. Because a raw C02 send does not fire the client's AttackEvent, the module calls the event manually and only attacks if it is not cancelled. Multi mode walks a path per target. mc.timer.timerSpeed accelerates the whole cycle.
modules.vanilla_hook: PreMotionEvent for the attack cycle; AttackEvent called manually before the C02 send.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The unconfirmed C04 walk is the tell: skipping the path or sending it too fast trips the vanilla 'moved too quickly' check, and position-disabler anti-cheats flag the round trip. Freecam interaction (attacking from the freecam origin) adds a second, larger anomaly.
modules.variations: Memeware's TPAura sends ATTACK directly via sendQueue with no pathfinding. Rise 6.x TeleportAura uses PacketUtil.sendNoEvent with one position packet per leg and no timer boost. Tenacity's TPAura uses addToSendQueue with a target walk and C02 ATTACK.

modules.name: ComboOneHit
modules.purpose: Kill in the Combo gamemode by sending dozens to thousands of ATTACK packets per swing.
modules.how_it_works: onAttackEvent fires after a normal attack and loops (int)packets.getValue() times (50 default, 1000 max), each iteration sending C02 ATTACK via sendPacketWithoutEvent so the flood never re-triggers attack listeners. The server processes every packet as a valid hit because vanilla applies no per-tick attack cap.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Pure rate abuse: any anti-cheat that caps hits-per-second or damage-per-tick kills it. It survives only on servers with no attack-rate validation, which is the Combo gamemode's defining weakness.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 ship the identical module with PacketUtil.send, the 6.x equivalent of sendPacketWithoutEvent.

modules.name: TriggerBot / Wtap
modules.purpose: Attack whatever the crosshair is on the instant the client raytrace hits an entity, and automate the W-tap sprint reset around attacks.
modules.how_it_works: TriggerBot checks mc.objectMouseOver on every EventMotion; when the raytrace type is ENTITY and the APS timer elapsed, it swings and queues C02 ATTACK via addToSendQueue. Wtap hooks EventSendPacket, and on any outgoing ATTACK with food above 6 queues STOP_SPRINTING then START_SPRINTING (C0B) so the server-side sprint reset happens around every hit, recreating the manual W-tap that resets the attack cooldown in 1.8 combat.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventMotion for TriggerBot; EventSendPacket on C02 for Wtap.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: TriggerBot is the hardest attack method to flag because it fires only when the player's own crosshair is on the target and carries no rotation anomaly; the APS cap is the only server-visible pattern. Wtap's C0B stop/start pair is a normal vanilla sequence and is invisible to anti-cheats.
modules.variations: No other client in the corpus ships a standalone TriggerBot for this packet; Spicy's AutoClicker is the same idea driven by mouse state and held-item checks, and its Killaura reuses the C02 path with full rotation injection.

general_hooks: The universal hook is the outgoing-packet event (PacketOutEvent, PacketSendEvent, EventSendPacket) matched against C02PacketUseEntity, usually by getAction() == ATTACK. Attack triggers also hang off UpdateEvent/PreMotionEvent (aim and swing) and Rise's dedicated AttackEvent, which Criticals and ComboOneHit consume.
client_variations: Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy and Tenacity queue C02 through mc.thePlayer.sendQueue.addToSendQueue. Rise 5.99 uses PacketUtil.sendPacket (event-routed) or PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent (bus-bypassing). Rise 6.x uses PacketUtil.send and PacketUtil.sendNoEvent. Sigma and Spicy also have a sendPacketNoEvent path through NetworkManager used by the INTERACT_AT disabler sequences.
